opportunities.title: AI governance + verification workflow
opportunities.wedge: Embed confidentiality, privilege, source verification and human-review rules directly into the legal AI workflow instead of leaving them in a policy PDF.
opportunities.buyer: Law firm managing partner, innovation lead or general counsel.
opportunities.painMoment: Lawyers are already using AI, but the firm cannot see whether use is safe, consistent or reviewable.
opportunities.firstTest: Audit one firm's real AI use, define three governed workflows and measure adoption plus review failures.
opportunities.fitNote: Excellent AI governance and workflow fit, with legal ethics partner needed.

evidence.title: ABA: 2026 legal AI adoption and governance gap
evidence.note: 69% of legal professionals report GenAI use while firm training, governance and trust lag behind.

evidence.title: ABA: AI and legal profession structural shift
evidence.note: AI efficiency increases pressure on established legal workflows and business models.

opportunities.title: AI-era matter pricing + fee redesign
opportunities.wedge: Use task decomposition, historical effort and AI-assisted production assumptions to price matters around value and risk rather than inherited billable-hour habits.
opportunities.buyer: Law firm leadership and practice-group heads.
opportunities.painMoment: AI cuts the time, but our revenue model still rewards time spent.
opportunities.firstTest: Reprice one repeatable matter type using retrospective data and compare margin/client acceptance with hourly pricing.
opportunities.priceHypothesis: US$10k-50k pricing redesign or analytics subscription
opportunities.fitNote: Strong business-model/product strategy fit.

evidence.title: ABA: law firm economics and what clients buy
evidence.note: AI exposes tension between client outcomes and billable-hour economics; firms are slow to change fee arrangements.

evidence.title: ABA: AI makes time a weaker proxy for value
evidence.note: Agentic and generative AI can dramatically reduce time required for core legal work.

opportunities.title: Verified matter + precedent retrieval
opportunities.wedge: Retrieve prior work product, clauses, positions and outcomes with matter context, provenance and explicit confidence rather than a generic semantic search box.
opportunities.buyer: Mid-size and large law firms.
opportunities.painMoment: We know the firm has solved this before, but finding the right precedent still depends on who remembers where it lives.
opportunities.firstTest: Index one practice group's closed matters and compare retrieval time/quality with current search.
riskNotes: Retrieval accuracy and provenance are critical.
opportunities.fitNote: Very strong knowledge architecture and AI retrieval fit.

evidence.title: ABA 2026 legal AI usage
evidence.note: Legal professionals widely use GenAI for research, drafting and summarization while trust and governance remain concerns.

evidence.title: ABA Legal Industry Report 2025
evidence.note: Firms prioritize legal AI that integrates with existing systems and trusted workflows.

opportunities.title: Billing + time leakage detector
opportunities.wedge: Find unbilled work, narrative problems, delayed time entry and matter-budget drift before invoices become write-offs.
opportunities.buyer: Law firm COO/CFO and practice leaders.
opportunities.painMoment: We did the work, but realization falls because time capture and billing quality break downstream.
opportunities.firstTest: Audit three months of time and invoice adjustments for one practice group and quantify avoidable leakage.
opportunities.priceHypothesis: US$2k diagnostic + recurring percentage of recovered revenue
riskNotes: Incentives around time capture can be political.
opportunities.fitNote: Strong analytics and operational-diagnostic fit.

evidence.title: ABA Legal Industry Report: AI in billing and firm operations
evidence.note: Legal professionals show interest in AI for billing, scheduling and financial insights.

evidence.title: ABA law firm economics 2026
evidence.note: Firm economics are under pressure as AI changes how legal work is produced and bought.

opportunities.title: Matter intake + conflict workflow orchestrator
opportunities.wedge: Turn client intake, conflicts, engagement terms, KYC and initial matter scoping into one observable workflow with clear blockers.
opportunities.buyer: Law firms with fragmented intake across email, forms and practice-management tools.
opportunities.painMoment: A potentially good matter stalls because five internal checks happen in different systems and nobody owns the queue.
opportunities.firstTest: Map intake cycle time for one firm and automate only handoffs/blocker visibility.
opportunities.fitNote: Excellent workflow/service design fit with clear system boundaries.

evidence.title: ABA 2025 legal technology report
evidence.note: Law firms increasingly seek AI and software that fit legal-specific workflows and firm operations.

evidence.title: ABA 2026 AI governance report
evidence.note: Institutional readiness and workflow structure lag individual AI adoption.

opportunities.title: AI workflow change-management system
opportunities.wedge: Map accounting tasks by risk, judgment and automation readiness, then make new AI workflows observable, reviewable and trainable.
opportunities.buyer: CPA firm leadership and transformation teams.
opportunities.painMoment: We bought AI tools, but adoption, quality control and staff behavior still vary by team.
opportunities.firstTest: Transform one repeatable workflow in one office and measure cycle time, review corrections and adoption.
riskNotes: Firm policies vary by service line.
opportunities.fitNote: Very strong AI operations and change-design fit.

evidence.title: AICPA 2026 Top Firm Issues Survey
evidence.note: Technology/AI change management ranks as a top long-term issue across accounting-firm sizes.

evidence.title: AICPA Profession Ready Initiative
evidence.note: AICPA launched a research-backed initiative for an increasingly AI-driven workplace.

opportunities.title: Client document collection + exception chase
opportunities.wedge: Turn missing documents, unanswered questions and inconsistent uploads into a single client-facing checklist and firm-side exception queue.
opportunities.buyer: Tax, bookkeeping and CAS firms.
opportunities.painMoment: The work is blocked not by accounting judgment but because three clients still have not sent the right statements.
opportunities.firstTest: Run one tax/close cycle with structured missing-item tracking and measure staff chasing time.
riskNotes: Many practice-management products partially cover portals.
opportunities.fitNote: Excellent interaction/workflow fit with low domain-risk boundary.

evidence.title: AICPA 2026 technology and workload issues
evidence.note: Technology integration and managing staff workload are major firm issues.

evidence.title: AICPA Profession Ready research
evidence.note: Accounting work is changing as automation reshapes traditional entry-level and recurring tasks.

opportunities.title: Busy-season workload + review-capacity planner
opportunities.wedge: Forecast work by client complexity, due date, reviewer bottleneck and staff skill rather than just open engagements.
opportunities.buyer: CPA firm operations leaders and partners.
opportunities.painMoment: The bottleneck is not total headcount; it is the right reviewer at the wrong week.
opportunities.firstTest: Model one firm's upcoming filing/close cycle and compare forecasted bottlenecks with actual overtime and delays.
riskNotes: Engagement complexity is hard to normalize.
Existing practice tools may contain incomplete data.
opportunities.fitNote: Strong capacity-planning and operations fit.

evidence.title: AICPA 2026 Top Firm Issues Survey
evidence.note: Managing staff workload and retention/recruitment remain prominent accounting-firm issues.

evidence.title: AICPA Profession Ready Initiative
evidence.note: The profession is actively rethinking talent models and skills in an AI-driven market.

opportunities.title: Close + reconciliation exception copilot
opportunities.wedge: Automate matching and routine reconciliation while surfacing only explainable exceptions that require accountant judgment.
opportunities.buyer: CAS firms, controllers and finance teams.
opportunities.painMoment: People spend hours reviewing transactions that are fine because the system cannot separate routine from genuinely weird.
opportunities.firstTest: Replay a monthly close and measure how many human review actions can safely collapse into exceptions.
riskNotes: Financial accuracy and audit trail are mandatory.
opportunities.fitNote: Excellent exception-based AI product fit with strong verifiability requirements.

evidence.title: AICPA: AI and technology change management
evidence.note: Accounting firms identify technology integration as a top present and future operational issue.

evidence.title: AICPA workforce readiness research
evidence.note: Automation is changing tasks that historically built early-career experience and judgment.

opportunities.title: Early-career judgment training from real work
opportunities.wedge: Turn reviewed engagements and correction patterns into scenario-based training that teaches why an experienced reviewer changed the work.
opportunities.buyer: CPA firms and accounting employers.
opportunities.painMoment: AI is removing some junior tasks faster than firms are replacing the learning those tasks used to provide.
opportunities.firstTest: Convert 50 anonymized review notes into interactive cases and measure reviewer correction rates for a new cohort.
riskNotes: Learning outcomes take time to measure.
opportunities.fitNote: Strong interaction/learning design and AI case-generation fit.

evidence.title: AICPA: building a profession-ready CPA workforce
evidence.note: Automation is reshaping early-career tasks and the path by which accountants develop judgment.

evidence.title: AICPA Profession Ready Initiative
evidence.note: The initiative explicitly targets skills needed for an AI-driven accounting workplace.

opportunities.title: Maintenance triage + vendor orchestration
opportunities.wedge: Turn resident reports, photos, asset history, urgency and vendor capacity into a transparent queue with ownership and resolution evidence.
opportunities.buyer: Residential property managers and multifamily operators.
opportunities.painMoment: A small maintenance issue becomes a resident crisis because nobody can see status, urgency or vendor responsibility.
opportunities.firstTest: Operate a human-in-the-loop maintenance dispatcher for one 200-500 unit portfolio and measure resolution time plus repeat contacts.
opportunities.fitNote: Excellent service orchestration and resident-facing UX fit.

evidence.title: Multihousing operating expense survey
evidence.note: Repairs/maintenance, payroll, utilities, insurance and management are tracked as core property operating expenses.

evidence.title: NARPM Residential Resource 2026
evidence.note: NARPM maintains ongoing practice guidance for residential property-management operations.

opportunities.title: Property operating-cost anomaly radar
opportunities.wedge: Compare insurance, utilities, repairs, taxes, payroll and vendor spend by property and flag changes that are not explained by asset or occupancy differences.
opportunities.buyer: Multifamily owners and property-management companies.
opportunities.painMoment: Operating costs moved, but the portfolio report tells us what happened only after the month is closed.
opportunities.firstTest: Analyze 12 months of expenses across 20 properties and validate top anomalies with property managers.
opportunities.fitNote: Strong analytical diagnostic with excellent measurable ROI.

evidence.title: Multihousing Operating Expense Survey
evidence.note: Industry benchmarking explicitly covers insurance, taxes, utilities, maintenance, payroll and other operating costs.

evidence.title: MHA property management survey bundle
evidence.note: Operators pay for benchmark data on operating expenses and compensation, validating demand for portfolio comparisons.

opportunities.title: Property compliance + inspection calendar
opportunities.wedge: Unify inspections, licenses, safety checks, local rental rules and evidence into an asset-specific compliance graph.
opportunities.buyer: Property managers operating across municipalities.
opportunities.painMoment: The rule is not difficult; remembering which building needs which action under which local system is.
opportunities.firstTest: Build the compliance graph for one operator across one metro and measure missed/late tasks eliminated.
opportunities.fitNote: Excellent rules + service-design fit.

evidence.title: NARPM Residential Resource 2026
evidence.note: Professional property management requires ongoing operational and regulatory practice management.

evidence.title: Multihousing operating benchmark survey
evidence.note: Property operations are already managed through detailed recurring expense and asset benchmarks.

opportunities.title: Resident communication + escalation layer
opportunities.wedge: Collapse email, portals, calls and vendor updates into one resident-visible thread with SLA, ownership and escalation logic.
opportunities.buyer: Property-management firms and multifamily operators.
opportunities.painMoment: Residents contact us three times because they cannot tell whether anyone is actually handling the problem.
opportunities.firstTest: Run one building's service requests through a unified thread and measure repeat contacts plus satisfaction.
opportunities.fitNote: Direct interaction/service design fit.

evidence.title: NARPM Residential Resource 2026
evidence.note: Resident and owner communication remains a core property-management practice domain.

evidence.title: Multihousing operating expense benchmarks
evidence.note: Payroll and management costs make communication efficiency economically relevant.

opportunities.title: Unit turnover + make-ready coordinator
opportunities.wedge: Sequence inspection, scope, vendors, materials, leasing and evidence so vacant days do not accumulate between departments.
opportunities.buyer: Multifamily operators and property managers.
opportunities.painMoment: A unit is empty, but every day of delay is hidden across maintenance, vendors and leasing.
opportunities.firstTest: Track 30 turnovers and use a shared dependency view to reduce median ready-to-rent time.
opportunities.fitNote: Excellent dependency/workflow coordination fit.

evidence.title: Multihousing Operating Expense Survey
evidence.note: Repairs, maintenance, payroll, evictions and rent metrics demonstrate the measurable economics surrounding unit operations.

evidence.title: NARPM Residential Resource
evidence.note: Property-management practice resources cover the recurring operational work surrounding rental portfolios.

opportunities.title: Teacher admin-load reducer
opportunities.wedge: Identify repetitive planning, reporting, communication and documentation tasks that can be safely collapsed without automating teacher judgment.
opportunities.buyer: School districts, schools and teacher organizations.
opportunities.painMoment: Teaching is already demanding, then administrative work follows the teacher home.
opportunities.firstTest: Time-map 20 teachers for two weeks and automate the top two non-instructional workflows.
riskNotes: Student data and teacher trust require strong safeguards.
opportunities.fitNote: Strong workflow/interaction fit, weaker near-term buyer economics.

evidence.title: RAND: State of Public Education in 2026
evidence.note: Teachers report poorer well-being than similar workers; working too many hours remains a major stress source.

evidence.title: RAND: making teaching sustainable
evidence.note: Teachers report longer hours and greater work-life intrusion than similar working adults.

opportunities.title: Student behavior intervention coordinator
opportunities.wedge: Turn incidents, context, accommodations, family contact and intervention follow-through into a shared support workflow instead of isolated notes.
opportunities.buyer: Schools and districts.
opportunities.painMoment: The same behavior keeps recurring because every adult sees only one slice of the pattern.
opportunities.firstTest: Pilot with one grade team and measure repeated incidents plus staff coordination time.
riskNotes: Algorithmic labeling of children must be avoided.
opportunities.fitNote: Service-design opportunity, but use AI only for coordination, never student risk labeling without strong governance.

evidence.title: RAND 2026 education survey
evidence.note: Managing student behavior is teachers' top reported job-related stress source in 2026.

evidence.title: RAND teacher sustainability research
evidence.note: Poor working conditions and inflexibility are closely tied to teacher well-being.

opportunities.title: Absence follow-up workflow
opportunities.wedge: Coordinate attendance signals, family outreach, support services and next actions so chronic absence is treated as a case workflow, not just a count.
opportunities.buyer: School districts and student-support teams.
opportunities.painMoment: We know who is absent, but the actual follow-up across school, family and services is inconsistent.
opportunities.firstTest: Run a manually coordinated cohort for one school and compare return-to-attendance with existing outreach.
riskNotes: Prediction should not replace human support decisions.
opportunities.fitNote: Strong coordination and case-management design fit.

evidence.title: RAND: State of Public Education 2026
evidence.note: RAND identifies chronic absenteeism as a persistent headwind affecting teachers and students.

evidence.title: RAND State of the American Teacher
evidence.note: Teacher workload and student-support demands interact with poor well-being.

opportunities.title: Family communication triage + translation
opportunities.wedge: Turn scattered family messages into categorized, translated, assigned conversations while preserving teacher voice and escalation.
opportunities.buyer: Schools with multilingual or high-volume family communication.
opportunities.painMoment: Teachers are answering the same logistical questions across email, messaging apps and translated notes.
opportunities.firstTest: Pilot one school's non-sensitive communication queue and measure teacher response time.
riskNotes: Should not automate sensitive family conversations.
opportunities.fitNote: Excellent communication UX and multilingual AI fit.

evidence.title: RAND 2026 teacher well-being data
evidence.note: Teacher time and workload remain significant stressors.

evidence.title: RAND sustainable teaching report
evidence.note: Work intrudes substantially into teachers' personal lives, increasing value of reducing non-instructional load.

opportunities.title: AI-era assignment + assessment design system
opportunities.wedge: Help teachers redesign tasks around observable process, oral defense, iteration and authentic evidence instead of trying to detect AI after submission.
opportunities.buyer: Schools, districts and higher-education programs.
opportunities.painMoment: The assignment still assumes that producing the final text proves the student did the thinking.
opportunities.firstTest: Redesign one course's assessments and compare teacher grading confidence plus student learning evidence.
opportunities.fitNote: Excellent interaction/assessment redesign fit.

evidence.title: RAND 2026 public education survey
evidence.note: Educators face multiple simultaneous student and workforce headwinds.
